title: chronological-cohort-release-with-rollback-simulation-harness
content:
description:
Context: We need a safer, deterministic way to promote model variants across time-ordered cohorts (e.g., night->morning->day) while being able to rehearse and validate rollback strategies offline. Current canary controllers focus on traffic fraction and random sampling; they make it hard to reproduce incidents tied to temporal cohort ordering and session-anchored users. Motivation: support product requests for time-windowed rollouts and to reduce noise in SLO regressions by deterministic cohort assignment. This PR introduces a chronological cohort release controller plus a rollback simulation harness that can (1) simulate policy-driven failures, (2) run micro-bisect scenarios across cohorts, and (3) produce deterministic traces for postmortem and automated rollback policy tuning. Summary of changes: - controller/chronological_cohort_controller.py: new controller implementing time-window cohort phases, cohort fencing, and session affinity preservation. - sim/rollback_harness.go: a lightweight simulator that replays traces and injects policy failures (latency, error spike, partial degradations) and computes candidate rollback points. - policies/rollback_policy_v2.yaml: new policy document that maps multi-metric gates (latency, error, quality eval) to rollback decision types (gradual-drain, immediate-swap, staged-revert). - docs/rollouts/chronological-cohort.md: design doc and operator playbook for running offline rehearse and live promotions. - tests/e2e/chron-cohort-e2e.py: end-to-end smoke tests that run a simulated 3-cohort promotion with a forced late cohort regression and validate rollback decisions. - infra/helm/values-rollout.yaml: optional Helm knobs for enabling deterministic replay mode in Private deployments. Design highlights: - Deterministic cohort assignment: users are deterministically hashed into chronological cohorts with a TTL-aware binder so a user's cohort remains stable for the rollout window. - Time-window phases: cohorts are gated by absolute wall-clock windows and can be paused/resumed by operator or automated SLO gates. - Rollback rehearsal: the harness can run a replay of live traces with synthetic degradations and evaluate how the configured policy would have behaved, producing a replay report and recommended policy adjustments. - Micro-bisect mode: the harness supports a binary-search-like simulation to find minimal cohort sets required to reproduce an SLO regression, enabling targeted rollbacks without full revert. Compatibility and migration: - No breaking user-facing APIs. - Helm flag rollout.deterministicReplay=false by default. Operators can opt-in per-cluster. Testing and verification: - Added unit tests for cohort hash stability and TTL rebind behavior. - E2E smoke covers a full promotion + mid-progress rollback path. - Simulator comes with deterministic seed option to make runs reproducible. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and playbook added - [x] Implementation of controller and simulation harness - [x] Unit tests and smoke e2e - [x] Helm values and docs - [x] Perf baseline: controller adds ~2.6% CPU on control-plane pod under synthetic load - [x] Security review: no new secrets stored; harness runs with cluster-reader role - [x] Manual staging rollout validated on staging cluster (2026-02-10) Commits: - "init: chronological cohort controller and API surface" - "sim: rollback harness prototype with deterministic seed" - "policies: add rollback_policy_v2 and mapping docs" - "docs: chronological cohort operator playbook" - "tests: add e2e smoke and unit tests for TTL binder" - "infra/helm/values-rollout.yaml: optional Helm knobs for enabling deterministic replay mode in Private deployments." - "Makefile (targets to run harness and e2e)" CI summary: - CI run #1: unit tests failed (timing-sensitive test flakiness in cohort TTL binder) - investigation: non-deterministic sleep in test harness; replaced with deterministic clock stub - CI run #2: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e-smoke with mocked sim) - Size/perf checks: control-plane pod CPU delta measured in staging; dashboard link: https://internal.redwood/reports/rollout/cpu-delta/545210 (internal) Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-18 after approvals. Migration plan: ops will enable rollout.deterministicReplay on staging for 48 hours and run a suite of historical replays for the last 30 days of traffic. Known limitations and follow-ups: - The harness does not simulate KV cache warm starts; follow-up ticket ENG-4489 scheduled to add model-stateful replay. - Does not yet integrate with Optimize's quantization recommendations; follow-up ENG-4522. - We observed a small CPU increase in the controller; plan to optimize the binder to avoid repeated hash computations. Contact: Priya Nair (author) and Ethan Ross (owner for production rollout).

release_notes:
Adds a deterministic chronological-cohort release controller with an independent rollback simulation harness. No API changes for customers. Enables scheduled cohort promotions and offline rollback rehearsal for safety validation.

review_comments:
Ethan Ross: Important work — controller looks clean. One request: can the cohort binder expose a metrics tag for cohort_id to make SLO drilldowns easier?
Priya Nair: Added cohort_id tag to metrics in next commit and instrumented trace-id -> cohort mapping in logs.
Sofia Martinez: The micro-bisect API looks powerful but I'm worried about operator safety. Can we add a dry-run flag so the harness never issues writes in rehearsal mode?
Priya Nair: Dry-run flag added in sim harness; it runs in read-only trace replay by default. Documented in playbook.
Liam Zhang: CI caught a flaky test — good catch. After fix, e2e smoke passed locally. Approving pending squash.
CI Bot: unit tests passed, integration passed, e2e-smoke (mocked) passed.
